meta: If AI saw the test before taking it, can you still trust its score? AI learns from billions of pages online, and AI tests are online too. When a test slips into the training data, that's data contamination.

muc.title: What if the test leaks?
muc.text: Last time, AI took tests called benchmarks. But what if the test leaks ahead of time?

muc.title: Studying only the answers
muc.text: You know the story: someone sees the test early and just memorizes the answers. Sky-high score, but stuck as soon as the test changes.

muc.title: The test slips into the lessons
muc.text: AI learns from billions of pages of text online. And AI tests are also posted publicly online. So the test slips into the training data without anyone noticing. This is called data contamination.

muc.title: Remembering, not understanding
muc.text: AI has seen the test, so it gets answers right by remembering, not understanding. Change a few numbers in the questions, and the score can drop sharply.

muc.title: When a number becomes the goal
muc.text: There's a rule named after the economist Goodhart: when a number becomes the goal, it stops measuring well. If everyone races for scores, scores go up, but real skill may not.

muc.title: New tests, hidden tests
muc.text: That's why people keep writing new tests after AI has finished learning. Some tests are even kept secret and never posted online, so AI can't see them ahead of time.

muc.title: Don't trust a single number
muc.text: Don't choose an AI just because of one number in an ad. Look at several reviews, then try it on your own work for a few days.

muc.title: Grading without a test?
muc.text: So is there a way to grade AI without a test at all? See you in part 3.
